QUIC bandwidth test with virtual client-server pair, loss/reorder emulation, and throughput logging

# Purpose
This file is a QUIC integration test and performance exercise for the `fd_quic` implementation. It creates a client and a server in the same process, connects them with `fd_quic_virtual_pair`, and can add network emulation with packet loss or reordering through `fd_quic_netem`. The test drives both endpoints with repeated calls to `fd_quic_service`, waits for the handshake to complete, opens a stream, sends data, and checks that the connection stays active while data flows. It also measures receive and transmit counters and prints periodic throughput information.

The file defines the callback functions used by the QUIC stack during connection and stream events, such as [`my_connection_new`](<#my_connection_new>), [`my_handshake_complete`](<#my_handshake_complete>), [`my_stream_rx_cb`](<#my_stream_rx_cb>), and [`my_conn_final`](<#my_conn_final>). The [`main`](<#main>) function sets up the clock, random number generator, workspace, and QUIC limits for both roles, then runs the full connection life cycle from handshake to stream transfer to orderly close. It ends by checking final metrics and cleaning up all allocated objects.
